messages:
emma: Quick note from the nightly run: after the selector tweak (prefer micro-kernels for short seqs) we’re seeing host ingress p99 climb ~14% on small requests. Flamegraphs show tokenization + http/gRPC header work dominating.

jorge: Any flame/top info? gRPC or HTTP/2 more affected?

emma: gRPC slightly worse. Top lines from pprof sample: 
``
31.2% Tokenizer::scan_utf8_chunks
22.7% grpc::header_parser::parse_chunk
11.8% host::preparse::emit_memmove
7.4% runtime::kvcache::lookup_miss
```
writev count per request increased ~3x in smallwrite traces.

priya: That sounds like fewer things getting batched on the GPU so host work is amortized less. Which kernel-selector change caused it?

emma: kernel-selector v3.2 lowered the sequence affinity so micro-kernel path is chosen for sequences < 40 tokens. Average batch size on our small-rt traffic went from 8.9 -> 5.3.

jorge: Two amplifiers then: smaller batches and more unique cache keys per batch. Have we measured kvcache hit rate?

emma: Yes — hit rate fell 0.93 -> 0.86 on repro. Eviction rate rose ~2x. Looks like smaller batch shapes increase unique key churn.

priya: Immediate mitigations? Can we: 1) revert selector cutoff, 2) coalesce header frames in host, 3) reuse tokenizer buffers to avoid allocs.

emma: I prototyped two host changes: thread-local tokenizer scratch (8k reuse) and header-frame coalescing for small consecutive frames (<=512B, within 2ms). Microbench results: token CPU -16%, header-parse calls -45%, writev syscalls down ~38% on smallwrite sim.

jorge: Nice. What about kvcache config? Increasing shards or TTL could help hit rate without touching kernels.

emma: I tried bumping per-shard capacity + TTL 5s->10s on a subset; hit rate recovered to 0.90 and p99 improved ~3% vs revert. Combined with the header patch we nearly get back to baseline tail. Quick numbers:
``
baseline: p99=185ms, p50=24ms, kvcache=0.93
selector-3.2: p99=211ms, p50=25ms, kvcache=0.86
3.2 + host-patches + kvcache-bump: p99=190ms, p50=25ms, kvcache=0.90
```
Not perfect but much better.

priya: Sounds like a short-term plan: roll host patches + kvcache config to canary, revert selector cutoff, then re-evaluate. Long-term we should add host-cost optics to kernel-selector so it can trade GPU efficiency vs host preparse cost.

emma: Agreed. I'll open PRs: one for tokenizer_buffer reuse + coalesce, one for kvcache config change, and a rollback PR for selector cutoff. Also adding a perf-suite replay that simulates many small requests (median tokens=6, payload~220B) to guard future selector changes.

perf-bot: perf-suite alert created: smallwrite_tail_increase at 2026-03-23T07:02:00Z -> alert_id 6139990001. Replay job scheduled.

jorge: Can we add a lightweight flamegraph snapshot step to every selector rollout? If we detect host-preparse % > threshold, fail the rollout.

emma: Yes — adding a rollout checklist item + automation in the rollout job to capture a 30s flame snapshot and compare against baseline. Action items: emma (PRs + perf replay), priya (spec host-cost signals for selector), jorge (add flamegraph step to rollout). tagging @pri ya @jorge for visibility :eyes:
